answers.core: Basic building block data structures offer a lot of bank for buck when it comes to programming. If Sets were to eventually become first-class in the language, they would need deep integration with it.
answers.workaround: I am meaning to make a Set class that uses Dictionaries under the hood so I can at least have a clean interface to work with for when I'm going to invariably move this to a C++ module. It is 100% work-around-able. As for how often Sets are used, I find that once you work on a project that needs them, you use them A LOT.
